correctness.rationale: For fixed d>=6, d(mu_m±s_m)=d±sqrt(2d)+[2d±(d+6)sqrt(2d)/2]/m+O_d(m^-2). Conditioning on W=chi_m^2/m yields E H_d(tW)=H_d(t)+t^2 f_d'(t)/m+O_d(m^-2) using EW−1=0, E(W−1)^2=2/m and fourth-moment/tail control. In each moving endpoint the exact first coefficient b_±+(d/2−1)t_±−t_±^2/2=±2sqrt(2d). Subtraction gives 2sqrt(2d)[f_d(t_+)+f_d(t_-)]/m>0; t_->0 for d>=6. Consequently C_{d,m} exceeds the chi-square limit for all sufficiently large m, pointwise in d. Independently rederived both symbolic identities using SymPy (R1_F_ENDPOINT_IDENTITY_OK); finite F distribution regression in source is not used as infinite proof.
residual_risks: No effective or d-uniform M_d and no all-m comparison.
Taylor remainder requires the fixed t_± positive, uniform derivatives on a fixed neighborhood of W=1 and exponentially small chi-square tails; these conditions hold at each fixed d>=6.

value.rationale: The one-standard-deviation probability conjecture is a stated nontrivial distribution-comparison problem. A positive sign in the leading finite-m correction proves the previously untreated high-denominator tail for every fixed numerator degree >=6, not merely a numerical fit. Exact density endpoint coefficient quantifies the approach and could be used in future uniformity/monotonicity work. The result explicitly does not claim all finite m or a uniform d threshold.
residual_risks: The improvement is only a pointwise asymptotic tail, not resolution of the full conjecture.

limitations: Fixed integer d>=6 only; m tends to infinity through m>=5.
Comparison to the Gaussian is via prior Gamma theorem, not independently reproved.
